results.title: Data Augmentation for Improving Explainability of Hate Speech Detection | Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering | Springer Nature Link
results.content: The paper presents a novel data augmentation-based approach to develop explainable, deep learning models for hate speech detection. Hate speech is widely prevalent on online social media but difficult to detect automatically due to challenges of natural language processing and complexity of hate speech. Further, the decisions of the existing solutions possess constrained explainability since limited annotated data are available for training and testing of models. Therefore, this work proposes the use of text-based data augmentation for improving the performance and explainability of deep learning models. Convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory models are trained with augmented data and evaluated on two publicly available datasets for hate speech detection. A diagnostic study is conducted on test samples to check for improvement in the models as a result of the data augmentation. ### Application of Data Augmentation Techniques for Hate Speech Detection with Deep Learning. In: Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Computational Linguistics, pp.

results.title: Enhancing cross-lingual hate speech detection through contrastive and adversarial learning - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Research paper Enhancing cross-lingual hate speech detection through contrastive and adversarial learning. To address the scarcity of labeled data in diverse languages, our approach adapts features from well-resourced languages to efficiently detect hate speech in low-resource contexts. We then introduce contrastive adversarial training, refining hate speech representations in low-resource languages. In many languages, especially those with limited resources, the absence of manually labeled data poses a significant challenge, not just in hate speech detection but also in the broader field of natural language processing. Given the challenges mentioned above, we propose a cross-lingual method based on supervised contrastive and adversarial training to learn similarities between cross-lingual hate speech datasets. Our assumption is that cross-lingual and multilingual representation improves hate speech detection performance, and aligning the representation spaces of several languages may enable the adaptation of features from well-resourced to poorly-resourced languages. Furthermore, applying a contrastive learning approach helps bridge multiple languages, promoting effective semantic alignment by learning sentence relationships between hate speech features in high- and low-resource languages. In our research, we leverage contrastive learning to develop a novel cross-lingual framework for hate speech detection, particularly focusing on low-resource languages such as Arabic, Persian, and Urdu. We aim to develop a more generalized and cross-lingual hate speech detection model, for which in-training data augmentation has proven to be a more suitable approach. We propose a novel cross-lingual contrastive learning framework specifically designed for hate speech detection in low-resource languages on social media. This framework leverages contrastive learning techniques to effectively capture nuanced representations of hate speech across diverse linguistic contexts, enabling improved detection capabilities in settings with limited labeled data. 2. We develop an innovative cross-lingual contrastive adversarial data augmentation framework to further enhance the representation of hate speech in low-resource contexts. We propose two frameworks to address the cross-lingual setting with contrastive learning and to adapt features captured from transfer learning between languages for detecting hate speech in low-resource languages. In this study, we introduced a novel cross-lingual and multilingual model specifically designed for hate speech detection in low-resource languages. ### Context-aware deep learning model for detection of roman urdu hate speech on social media platform.

results.title: Interpretable and High-Performance Hate and Offensive Speech Detection
results.content:
Title: Interpretable and High-Performance Hate and Offensive Speech Detection
Since detecting hate and offensive speech in social media platforms could incorrectly exclude individuals from social media platforms, which can reduce trust, there is a need to create explainable and interpretable models. For unbalanced Twitter data, XGboost outperformed the LSTM, AutoGluon, and ULMFiT models on hate speech detection with an F1 score of 0.75 compared to 0.38 and 0.37, and 0.38 respectively. When we down-sampled the data to three separate classes of approximately 5000 tweets, XGBoost performed better than LSTM, AutoGluon, and ULMFiT; with F1 scores for hate speech detection of 0.79 vs 0.69, 0.77, and 0.66 respectively. In this regard, different models have been built for hate and offensive speech detection but the majority of these are not interpretable or explainable. Several machine learning approaches, especially neural network systems, used in detecting hate and offensive speech demonstrate high performance but are not often explainable or interpretable [2]. Such hate and offensive speech detection models do not allow us to see which features contribute to the detection of a hate or offensive speech, key to building trust in such systems. Thus, when using XGBoost over neural networks, a hate and offensive speech detection model is more explainable and interpretable in describing which features have led to a particular class detection. Past research has used a limited number of features and we extend the literature by considering a comprehensive set of features to improve model performance, explainability, and interpretability, and ability to distinguish between hateful and offensive speech. RQ1: How can we make hate and offensive speech detection models more explainable and interpretable? and RQ2: How can we improve the performance of hate and offensive speech detection models? #### 2.0.1 Hate and Offensive Speech Detection Models. There exist several hate and offensive speech detection models [23]. In the offensive and hate class, XGBoost performed relatively better than the other models. To assist in coming up with models that can detect the two types of languages, we come up with our own XGBoost based high performance model that can detect hate speech and offensive speech. Upon down sampling our data, in the hate and offensive classes, XGBoost performed better than the other models.

results.content: Linguistic-based Data Augmentation Approach for Offensive Language Detection | IEEE Conference Publication | IEEE Xplore. # Linguistic-based Data Augmentation Approach for Offensive Language Detection. The massive amount of data generated by social media possess a great deal of toxic content that lead to serious content filtering problems including hate speech, cyberbul...Show More. The massive amount of data generated by social media possess a great deal of toxic content that lead to serious content filtering problems including hate speech, cyberbullying and insulting. That said, there is a growing need for a comprehensive and high-quality dataset in Turkish that can be utilized in development of NLP models for robust detection of offensive language usage in social media. Therefore, we propose a data augmentation approach based on data mining methods utilizing the linguistic features of Turkish that can help enhance the generalizability of machine learning models without further human interaction.
